You lived through a thousand days that you don't remember.
Your first steps. Your first word. Your first birthday cake.
Scientists call it infantile amnesia. And everyone has it.
Most people's earliest memory is from around age three.
So here's the big question. Were those memories ever saved?
For a long time, scientists thought the baby brain just wasn't recording.
Then, in 2025, researchers put babies inside a brain scanner.
They showed them pictures. A face. A toy. A beach.
Later, they showed some of the pictures again.
When a baby's memory centre lit up the first time, the baby stared longer at that picture the second time.
From about one year old, babies are already saving memories.
So maybe they're not deleted. Maybe they're just locked.
And in mice, scientists have already switched lost baby memories back on, with light.
So somewhere in your head, your first birthday might still be there.
You just don't have the key.
